scenarios.title: A creature with haste can attack the turn it comes under its controller's control

setup.notes: A's creature came under A's control this turn.

decisions: A checks whether its creature can be declared as an attacker.

variants.label: haste_creature
variants.expected: Raging Goblin (haste) is a legal attacker even though it has not been under A's control since the turn began.

variants.label: no_haste_creature
variants.delta: A's creature is Mons's Goblin Raiders (no haste) instead of Raging Goblin, also summoning sick.
variants.expected: Mons's Goblin Raiders is not a legal attacker.

scenarios.title: A creature with haste can use its tap-symbol ability the turn it comes under its controller's control

setup.notes: Prodigal Sorcerer came under A's control this turn. Fervor gives creatures its controller controls haste. The no_haste and opponent_controls_fervor variants remove Fervor from A's side or move it to B's.

decisions: A checks whether Prodigal Sorcerer's {T} ability can be activated, targeting player B.

variants.label: haste_from_fervor
variants.expected: Activating Prodigal Sorcerer's ability is legal for A although the creature is summoning sick, because it has haste from Fervor.

variants.label: no_haste
variants.delta: Fervor is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Activating Prodigal Sorcerer's ability is illegal: the creature is summoning sick and its cost includes {T}.

variants.label: opponent_controls_fervor
variants.delta: Fervor is on B's side of the battlefield instead of A's.
variants.expected: Activating Prodigal Sorcerer's ability is illegal: Fervor gives haste only to creatures B controls.
